comment: Every story line in the Level 1 demo, keyed by scene and line id.
notes: Code generated with AI assistance (Claude). Reviewed by team. PLACEHOLDER TEXT, copied from docs/Demo_Script_Full.md; the team is rewriting it. To rewrite a line, change its 'text' (and 'speaker' if needed) here and nothing else. Do NOT rename a scene or a line id: story_level1.json (which line plays when), pike_lines.json, npc_barks.json and facility_audio.json refer to lines as 'scene.line_id'. 'speaker' is a key of 'speakers' below (the name shown in the dialogue box); a line with no speaker is narration. Placeholders used by the script: surname 'Rhodes', project name '[NAME]'.

line_1.text: 1958. NASA is six months old. Everyone wants the Moon.

line_2.text: Walter Rhodes wanted it more than anyone. He designed Project SELENE: America's first crewed lunar landing.

line_4.text: On the night of his kid's science fair, he worked late again.

fight_2.speaker: dad
fight_2.text: The test ran long, kiddo, I'm sorry, I—

fight_3.speaker: kid
fight_3.text: You care more about that Moon than me.

fight_4.speaker: dad
fight_4.text: That's not… I'll explain. I promise.

line_5.text: Three weeks later, he was gone.

line_6.text: NASA shelved SELENE the same month. Too risky. Too expensive. Too much Walter.

line_7.text: Six months later, his kid walks through the front door.

mom_note.speaker: mom_note
mom_note.text: Be home for dinner. Please. It took him; don't let it take you too. Love, Mom.

guard_1.speaker: guard
guard_1.text: Badge? …Rhodes. Huh. Sorry about your dad, kid.

guard_2.speaker: guard
guard_2.text: Director Pike's waiting upstairs. Lift's down the hall.

brief_1.speaker: pike
brief_1.text: Rhodes. Your file says "clerk." Today it says "engineer." Don't get excited.

brief_2.speaker: pike
brief_2.text: Our satellite team ate the cafeteria fish. You're building BEACON-1.

brief_3.speaker: pike
brief_3.text: Twenty kilograms in orbit. Transmitting for thirty days.

brief_4.speaker: pike
brief_4.text: Fifteen million dollars. Not a cent more. I check.

brief_5.speaker: pike
brief_5.text: Design Bay's downstairs. Dot will show you around. Try not to explode anything.

photo.speaker: photo
photo.text: An old photo: Pike and Walter at a launch, both grinning.

after_photo_1.speaker: pike
after_photo_1.text: …He was the best engineer I ever worked with. And I didn't listen to him once when it mattered.

after_photo_2.speaker: pike
after_photo_2.text: Get out of my office, Rhodes.

refuse_1.speaker: pike
refuse_1.text: That's not in the budget, Rhodes.

refuse_2.speaker: pike
refuse_2.text: Do I look like I'm made of money? Don't answer that.

refuse_3.speaker: pike
refuse_3.text: Fifteen million. I can count. Can you?

intro_1.speaker: dot
intro_1.text: You're Walter's kid. You've got his frown.

intro_2.speaker: dot
intro_2.text: Mug number six. Don't touch it.

intro_3.speaker: dot
intro_3.text: Rule one: the rocket has to fly straight. Heavy stuff up front, fins at the back, like an arrow.

intro_4.speaker: dot
intro_4.text: Rule two: enough fuel to get where you're going. Rockets mostly carry fuel to carry fuel.

intro_5.speaker: dot
intro_5.text: Rule three: one stage won't make orbit. Nobody's does. Stack them.

intro_6.speaker: dot
intro_6.text: Build it on the bench. Then take it upstairs to the IBM. The computer doesn't lie. People do.

fb_stable_good.speaker: dot
fb_stable_good.text: Look at that. Your dad would've signed off on it. …Eventually.

fb_wobbly.speaker: dot
fb_wobbly.text: It'll fly like a drunk pigeon. Bigger fins, or move weight up front.

fb_tumbles.speaker: dot
fb_tumbles.text: That's not a rocket, that's a pinwheel. Fins. Back. Bigger.

fb_over_stable.speaker: dot
fb_over_stable.text: Too much fin. It'll turn into the wind like a weathervane.

fb_not_enough_fuel.speaker: dot
fb_not_enough_fuel.text: You'll get halfway to orbit and then visit the ocean.

fb_too_heavy.speaker: dot
fb_too_heavy.text: It's not leaving the pad. Lighter, or more engine.

fb_ready.speaker: dot
fb_ready.text: Run it through the IBM. Then we talk launch.

about_dad_1.speaker: dot
about_dad_1.text: Walter hired me when nobody else would. Brought two coffees every morning, one for me. Every day.

about_dad_2.speaker: dot
about_dad_2.text: He kept a model rocket on his desk. Said a kid designed the fins. Never told me which kid.

jo_1.speaker: jo
jo_1.text: You're Walt's kid. I'm Jo. I was going to fly SELENE.

jo_2.speaker: jo
jo_2.text: Your dad stayed up three nights straight checking my oxygen numbers. Three. Nobody does that.

jo_3.speaker: jo
jo_3.text: He talked about you more than the Moon. Don't let anyone tell you different.

jo_return.speaker: jo
jo_return.text: Go build something, kid. I'll be watching from mission control.

coffee_pot.speaker: coffee_pot
coffee_pot.text: Nearly empty. A note: "DOT'S. TOUCH AND DIE."

operator_intro.speaker: operator
operator_intro.text: Punch your numbers, feed the deck, wait for the whir. Don't drop the cards. Ever.

operator_after_printout.speaker: operator
operator_after_printout.text: Machine's happy. That's one of us.

slide_rule.text: Has anyone seen my slide rule?

card_deck.text: The IBM ate my card deck again.

fins_at_back.text: Fins at the back. Always fins at the back.

booster_hallway.text: Who parked a booster in the hallway?

fish.text: Attention: the cafeteria fish has been… discontinued.

slide_rule.text: Would the owner of a blue slide rule report to the IBM room.

hazard_drill.text: Reminder: launch hazard drill at fifteen hundred.

capcom_go.speaker: capcom
capcom_go.text: Flight, we are GO for launch.

success_dot.speaker: dot
success_dot.text: Mug number six. You can touch it. Once.

fail_fell_short.speaker: fido
fail_fell_short.text: We're not going to make orbit… she's coming back down.

fail_dot_after.speaker: dot
fail_dot_after.text: Hey. Your dad lost one like this. He didn't sleep for a week. Then he fixed it. Try again.

brass_key.speaker: brass_key
brass_key.text: A brass key. Tag says "W.R." in Dot's handwriting.

obj_nameplate.speaker: nameplate
obj_nameplate.text: W. RHODES, LEAD DESIGNER, PROJECT SELENE. Someone scratched SELENE off.

obj_moon_poster.speaker: moon_poster
obj_moon_poster.text: Covered in pencil notes. Landing sites circled. One is labelled "for the kid."

obj_model_rocket.speaker: model_rocket
obj_model_rocket.text: Hand-built. One fin snapped off. It looks a lot like the one you made for the science fair.

obj_photo.speaker: photo
obj_photo.text: You, age seven, in a cardboard space helmet. Dad's laughing.

obj_mugs.speaker: mugs
obj_mugs.text: Four of them. All empty. All from the same night.

obj_calendar.speaker: calendar
obj_calendar.text: Every day crossed out, up to one. The science fair. Circled twice. Not crossed out.

obj_drawer.speaker: drawer
obj_drawer.text: Locked. A label reads "SELENE: FINAL." You'll need a key.

tape1_1.speaker: dad_tape
tape1_1.text: Log one. It's 2 a.m. Coffee number four. Don't tell your mother.

tape1_2.speaker: dad_tape
tape1_2.text: Every rocket has a number: how much it can lift. Respect the number.

tape2_1.speaker: dad_tape
tape2_1.text: Log nine. Pike signed off on the cheaper heat shield. I told him it'll fail.

tape2_2.speaker: dad_tape
tape2_2.text: He said the budget's the budget. …I'm going to fix it myself. Even if it takes every night I have.

tape3_1.speaker: dad_tape
tape3_1.text: Log fourteen. Missed the fair. I keep missing things.

tape3_2.speaker: dad_tape
tape3_2.text: Ruth says I'm building a rocket to escape the house. Maybe she's right.

tape3_3.speaker: dad_tape
tape3_3.text: But it's not for me. One day I'll tell the kid what it's really for.

tape3_4.speaker: dad_tape
tape3_4.text: …I saw the photo. Your fins were better than ours. I promise I'll explain.

launch.text: Go to Mission Control and launch

poll_override.speaker: flight
poll_override.text: NO-GO on the loop. It's your call, Flight.

poll_hold.text: Launch held. Fix the NO-GO items, then poll the room again.
